note: Studies confirm distinct TUBA4A missense variants cause spastic ataxia (SPAX11) with variable onset and altered microtubule dynamics rather than classic ALS.

evidence.text: Screening of ataxia cohorts identified ultra-rare TUBA4A missense variants causing hereditary spastic ataxia with variable age of onset, where cultured patient fibroblasts demonstrated significant alterations in microtubule organization and dynamics.

source.title: De novo and inherited monoallelic variants in TUBA4A cause ataxia and spasticity
source.quote: Cultured fibroblasts from three patients harbouring distinct TUBA4A missense showed significant alterations in microtubule organization and dynamics, providing insight of TUBA4A variants pathogenicity. Our data confirm the identification of a hereditary spastic ataxia disease gene with variable age of onset, expanding the clinical spectrum of TUBA4A associated phenotypes.

numbers.metric: patients presenting with spasticity and/or cerebellar ataxia harbouring TUBA4A missense mutation

evidence.text: Specific dominant TUBA4A mutations associate with SPAX11 and congenital myopathy rather than amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, demonstrating variant- and cell-type-specific divergence without motor neuron degeneration.

source.title: A mouse model of autosomal dominant spastic ataxia and myopathy caused by a mutation in Tuba4a
source.quote: Dominant TUBA4A mutations in humans are associated with spastic ataxia type 11 (SPAX11), congenital myopathy type 26 (CMYO26), and frontotemporal dementia/amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 9 (FTDALS9). Our mice exhibit hallmark features of SPAX11 and CMYO26, but do not show motor neuron degeneration.
